name: Motorized Bulldozer
instructions: omr/instructions/8275-1-3.pdf (book 1/3: the functions are drawn on pages 5, 8 and 9), 8275-1-2.pdf (book 2/3) and 8275-1-1.pdf (book 3/3: blade steps 73-76, ripper steps 77-79); the files are numbered in the opposite order to the books

functions.does: The left XL motor drives the left track: a 16 tooth gear on its shaft drives, through a 16 tooth idler and another 16 tooth gear, a 12 tooth bevel gear that turns the 20 tooth gear on the axle of the left front sprocket.
functions.source: book 1 page 5 (the two XL motors, marked 5) and page 8 (the drive remote, marked 6); the gears are inferred from the model
functions.note: The motor (p136 58121) turns the control, its 16 tooth gear on the motor's shaft. It is worked from the IR remote with its channel switch set as marked 6 on book 1 page 8, one lever for each track.

functions.does: The right XL motor drives the right track the same way, from the back: a 16 tooth gear on its shaft drives, through a 16 tooth idler and another 16 tooth gear, a 12 tooth bevel gear that turns the 20 tooth gear on the axle of the right rear sprocket.
functions.source: book 1 pages 5 and 8; the gears are inferred from the model
functions.note: The motor (p733 58121) turns the control, its 16 tooth gear on the motor's shaft.

functions.does: With both tracks driven the same way the bulldozer drives straight forwards or back; with one track driven it turns; with the tracks driven opposite ways it spins on the spot.
functions.source: book 1 page 8 (the four pictures across the top)

functions.does: The six pistons of the V6 engine in the middle of the bulldozer pump in their cylinders as it drives: the left track's drive turns the crankshaft through 12 and 20 tooth double bevel gears.
functions.source: book 1 page 8 (inset 9 shows the pistons moving); that it runs off the left track's drive is inferred from the model's gears (p15 32270, p23 32270, p1437 32269, p1443 32270)
functions.note: Unsure which track's drive works the engine; the gears in the model join it to the left one.

functions.does: One M motor raises and lowers the blade: an 8 tooth gear on its shaft drives a 24 tooth clutch gear, then 16 tooth gears up and forward to a worm at the front, which turns the 24 tooth gear on a cross axle; bent liftarms on that axle pull the blade up through links on both sides, and the long yellow push arms pivot on the frame.
functions.source: book 1 pages 5 (M motors, marked 4) and 9 (lower remote picture: blade up and down); book 3 steps 73-76 (blade fitted); the gear train is inferred from the model
functions.note: The motor (p1834 58120, on the left) turns the control, its 8 tooth gear. Worked from the remote with its channel switch set as marked 7 on book 1 page 9. Unsure which M motor is which: by the model's gears the left one lifts the blade and the right one the ripper.

functions.does: The other M motor raises and lowers the ripper at the back: an 8 tooth gear on its shaft drives a 24 tooth clutch gear whose shaft runs back through a universal joint to a worm, which turns a 24 tooth gear that swings the ripper's parallel arms up and down.
functions.source: book 1 pages 5 and 9 (top pictures: ripper up and down, remote channel marked 7); book 3 steps 77-79 (ripper fitted); the gear train is inferred from the model
functions.note: The motor (p1605 58120, on the right) turns the control, its 8 tooth gear.

functions.does: The two 24 tooth clutch gears slip when the blade or the ripper reaches the end of its travel, so the M motors can keep running without breaking anything.
functions.source: inferred: what the 24 tooth clutch gears (p121 76019, p1261 76019) do in these drives; the book doesn't say
